reasons: Form behaviour is outside this file.

terms.meaning: A crew that people can join only with a code from a member.

used_by: Next.js route for /crews (no importing file visible)

sections.name: File setup, metadata
sections.title: Imports and tab title
sections.what: Brings in the link component, the user helper, the crew list function and the forms component. Sets the tab title to Your crews.
sections.why: Needed to load the list and show the forms.

sections.name: CrewsPage
sections.title: Crew list and empty message
sections.what: Gets the user's crews and shows either an empty message or one tile per crew with its name and member count, marking crews the user owns. Then shows the forms.
sections.why: Likely reason: the list and the actions sit on one screen.
sections.watch_out: The wording switches between member and members based on a count of one, so the count must be a real number.

summary: Lists the signed-in person's crews with member counts, and shows forms to create or join one.
purpose: The entry point for crews: shows what crews the user is in and lets them start or join one.
why: Reason not stated in the code for the layout. The text says crews are invite-only.
how: Loads the user's crews. If there are none, shows a friendly message. Otherwise shows a tile per crew with its name, member count and an owner note, then shows the create and join forms.
inputs: The signed-in user and the crew list from listMyCrews.
outputs: Crew tiles that link to each crew, or an empty message, plus the forms.
risks: Form validation lives in another file that is not shown here. Member counts come from the service without checks in this file.
debug: If crews are missing, check listMyCrews. If forms misbehave, check the CrewForms component.
